To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the method described here is useful for amplification of complex mixtures containing DNA fragments of less than 1 kb in size, starting from as low as 10 pg of DNA.
we report here proportional amplifications of DNA fragments that are first converted into concatemers starting from DNA amount as low as 0.1 pg.
we developed a new method for proportional amplification of complex mixtures composed of short DNA fragments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
development and application of an efficient and cost effective method to amplify minute amounts of complex DNA mixtures.
developing a method that allows for representative amplification of complex mixtures, which can be used for further genetic analyses.
development and optimization of a method that can be used to generate good quality and quantity of target DNA from a complex mixture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method described here allows for amplification of complex DNA mixtures from as low as 100 pg of DNA, and is a useful tool for high-throughput genomics.
the method described here is useful in amplifying short DNA fragments from complex mixtures, and is especially suitable for amplification from minute quantities of DNA.
the improved MDA method is useful for amplification of complex mixtures containing short DNA fragments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new method that is useful to generate long linear and circular DNA concatamers from minute amounts of input DNA, starting from as low as 10 pg, which can be subsequently amplified using phi29 polymerase to generate sufficient material for further analysis.
improved MDA is a useful method for amplifying DNA from a complex mixture and can be used for further downstream applications.
we developed an MDA protocol for the generation of high molecular weight DNA from complex mixtures of short DNA fragments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
religation at low concentrations (< 1 ng/uL) should be avoided as this leads to preferential self-circularization of the fragments.
religation at a concentration of > 10 ng /μ L, in presence of a stuffer DNA is a prerequisite for obtaining uniform amplification of complex mixtures.
religation at a high concentration of DNA, in presence of stuffers, is the key to generate uniform amplification.
